answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying each identity to independently verified infrastructure diversity. Verifiers scattered worldwide measure round-trip latency and routing paths, so an agent claiming to wander across regions must prove it operates there; a cluster of fake identities spun up on one server farm shows identical timing fingerprints. Each fake then needs its own voyage through distinct networks and hardware, and at the nadir of cheap spoofing, when one machine pretends to be hundreds, the cost stops scaling for free and rises with every new location the attacker must rent.
